name: Idaho
sources: Rate 5.3% (HB 40, 2025), unchanged for 2026: Idaho HB 40 statement of purpose, https://legislature.idaho.gov/wp-content/uploads/sessioninfo/2025/legislation/H0040SOP.pdf and EY Tax News 2026-1829, https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1829

2025 zero-rate amounts $4,811 single/MFS, $9,622 joint/HoH/surviving spouse: Thomson Reuters Planner CS Idaho 2025 release notes, https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en-us/help/planner-cs/release-notes/idaho-2025-1-1 ; HoH/MFS grouping and itemizing rules: 2024 Form 40 instructions, https://tax.idaho.gov/wp-content/uploads/forms/EIN00046/EIN00046_10-23-2024.pdf

Conformity to federal OBBBA incl. enhanced senior deduction (HB 559, 2026, retroactive to 2025): https://www.kmvt.com/2026/02/12/idaho-governor-signs-bill-adopting-nearly-all-tax-changes-federal-big-beautiful-bill/ and https://www.kmvt.com/2026/03/04/idaho-taxpayers-can-now-file-2025-returns-claim-new-conformity-deductions
Idaho child tax credit sunset after 2025: Idaho State Tax Commission, https://tax.idaho.gov/pressrelease/withholding-tables-updated-for-2026/
Federal senior deduction ($6,000 per person 65+, reduced 6% of MAGI over $75,000 / $150,000 joint, not allowed MFS): IRC 151(d)(5)(C)
provisional: Zero-rate amounts ($4,811 single/MFS, $9,622 joint/HoH) are the 2025 values; Idaho indexes them annually and the 2026 amounts are not yet published.
Itemizing rules are from the 2024 Form 40 instructions; property tax is capped at the 2026 federal SALT cap ($40,400; $20,200 MFS) without the phase-down above $505,000 of income.
notes: Idaho's refundable food tax credit ($155 per person in 2025) is not included.
